body:
FROM T200's P5 REVIEW (three lenses, 2026-08-20). The findings that are DESIGN interactions rather
than repairs, parked here so the merge does not wait on them and none is lost.

1. A CONTEST ARRIVING LIVE TURNS A SERVED LENS INTO A BARE 404 (suppression lens, PLAUSIBLE).
Under declared `conflicts`, when a rival binding lands, readRegistrations drops both candidates and
the surface rebuilds correctly — but a reader who was resolving that lens yesterday now gets the
same answer as "no such lens ever existed". readContestedBindings exists and no DOOR serves it: the
name is not in the withdrawn set, so the §17 door answers 404 rather than 410-or-contest-notice. The
spec's "refusal a person can act on" is an API, not yet a door. Decide where the notice surfaces.

2. ADOPT-LAW'S NAME GUARD IS POLICY-BLIND (lens-name lens, PLAUSIBLE). schemaWinner takes
registrationVersions().at(-1) per lens — hardwired latest semantics regardless of the declared mode.
Under `conflicts` with a dark contested name, adoptLaw refuses with "already answered here by
DIFFERENT-content law" — the name is answered by NOTHING — and supersede negates only the
ground-latest contender, leaving the contest standing while reporting adopted-from. boundElsewhere
similarly witnesses against versions the policy resolves away. The guard should read the resolved
table, which slice 3's container-scoped bindings will already have to touch.

3. MANUAL REGISTRATIONS ARE INVISIBLE TO THE POLICY (lens-name lens, PLAUSIBLE). A process-local
manual registration holding a lens is not a candidate, so a `conflicts` store keeps serving a name
the operator declared contested, and readContestedBindings reports nothing. Whether config-borne
bindings are in-scope for §47 law is a design call; today the policy silently governs half the
contest space and no reader says so.

4. byAuthorRank IS VACUOUS UNTIL AGGREGATION (suppression lens, CONFIRMED, expected). In a governed
store every served binding is operator-authored, and ungoverned stores have no operator to rank by —
both regimes reduce to byTimestamp. Harmless now; a TRAP the moment any future path lands
non-operator bindings while an operator believes rank protection is active. Slice 3's aggregation is
where rank becomes real, and its door-level rail (criterion 5) must land IN THE SAME CHANGE that
makes non-operator bindings reachable, not after.

TIER: 1 and 3 are design calls (Myk); 2 rides slice 3's rework of the guard.

5. CROSS-PROGRAM SUPERSEDE TRIPS THE PUBLISH TRIAL (found writing the as-never-takes rail).
publishRegistrationImpl's `survivors` filter excludes only same-(program, lens) incumbents, so a
supersede that takes a name held by a DIFFERENT program's law meets the gql collision at the trial
build and refuses — while the same-program case (T33's rails) works. Under a declared policy the
trialSurvivors branch already excludes the cross-entity rival, so this bites only undeclared stores.
Either the supersede path should thread its negates into the trial set, or the refusal should say
"supersede across programs wants a declared policy" rather than a bare collision.
title: Policy-edge interactions from T200's review: the dark-name notice, the policy-blind guard, manual regs
